topics.title: [grug] Parse ROCm compute capabilities in the ragged all-to-all backend
topics.body:
The ragged all-to-all MoE backend checks for an SM100 GPU before choosing the QuACK grouped-GEMM expert MLP, and parsed the device's `compute_capability` as a float. ROCm devices report an architecture name such as `gfx942`, so every expert-parallel run with `--moe-impl ragged_all_to_all` on AMD failed with `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'gfx942'` while tracing the first step. Architecture names now count as not SM100, and the backend falls back to `ragged_dot` as it does on other non-Blackwell GPUs.

The backend still does not run on ROCm. With this change, the June Snowball model on 8× MI300X (JAX 0.11, ROCm 10) compiles and then fails in the first step with `UNIMPLEMENTED: Device communicator is not implementing`, which points to XLA's RCCL communicator lacking ragged all-to-all. The `ring` and `fixed_all_to_all` backends run on the same node.

Part of #9462.

topics.title: Skip S3 directory creation when writing FineStore shards
topics.body:
FineStore calls `mkdirs` before writing each shard to support local filesystems. S3 prefixes need no directory creation. When s3fs bucket checks fail, `mkdirs` attempts to create the existing bucket and can report `InvalidRegion`, hiding the original check errors.

Skipping `mkdirs` for S3 adds an S3-specific condition in FineStore. I looked for a way to preserve the underlying bucket-check error instead, but that appears to require patching s3fs.

Related issues:

- [Antidoom eval archive failure](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/616): this FineStore call reached `CreateBucket` and failed with `InvalidRegion`.
- [SkyRL checkpoint upload failure #9213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9213): s3fs directory creation reached the same error during training.
- [Compiler-cache recovery #9202](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9202): rclone required `--s3-no-check-bucket` to avoid `InvalidRegion`.

topics.title: zephyr: give each worker attempt its own worker ID
topics.body:
* fixes #9740
* zephyr worker ID now includes the iris attempt number: `<group>-<index>-a<attempt_id>` (`attempt_worker_id`)
* iris can start a new attempt of a lost worker task while the old attempt still runs; both used the same worker ID
  * the old attempt pulled a shard after the new one registered, then died, and the new attempt's heartbeats kept the shared ID alive, so the shard stayed in flight forever [^1]
* with one ID per attempt, each process has its own liveness:
  * a dead old attempt misses its heartbeats, and `check_heartbeats` requeues its shards (up to the 120 s timeout)
  * a live old attempt can finish its shards; the attempt check keeps the current result
* no RPC changes; outside iris (`get_job_info()` is `None`) the attempt is 0
* add `test_shard_of_a_dead_replaced_attempt_is_requeued_while_its_successor_lives`, which builds two `ZephyrWorker` attempts and fails with the shared ID
* side effects:
  * dead attempts stay in the coordinator maps as `FAILED`, so the `N/M workers alive, D dead` status line and the dashboard worker list grow with each replaced attempt
  * re-registration under the same ID now only covers a repeated registration from the same process [^2]

[^1]: seen 3 times on 2026-10-04 in the datakit ferry runs (tier 1 and tier 2), each after a preemptible v5e host was lost. The coordinator showed `105/106 complete, 1 in-flight, 1/1 workers alive` until the new attempt was preempted by hand.
[^2]: an earlier version of this PR fenced the old attempt with an incarnation token on `pull_task` and `heartbeat`. It needed checks on more RPCs: a replaced attempt that exits calls `deregister_worker` with the shared ID, which removed the current attempt's registration.

topics.title: [grug] AdamH produces NaNs for zero-norm parameters
topics.body:
The AdamH copies used by current and historical Grug divide by `norm(new_p)` without a floor. A zero-norm matrix produces a NaN update even at learning rate zero. This poisoned a 67B SFT checkpoint on its first warmup update; the next forward pass reported NaN loss.

Reproduce:
1. Create a zero `2 x 2` parameter and an all-ones gradient.
2. Build `experiments.grug.moe.adamh.scale_by_adamh(learning_rate=0.0)` and apply one update.
3. Observe that every returned update is NaN. The vendored `experiments.june_tpu_67b_a2b.moe.adamh` copy behaves identically, including for stacked matrices.

Expected: zero-norm parameters remain finite under AdamH, including during a zero-learning-rate warmup step.

comments.body: 🤖 https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9806 floors the updated matrix norm in `scale_by_adamh` at 1e-10 for the Grug MoE and hero FSDP copies. A zero matrix no longer produces a NaN update on a zero learning-rate or zero-gradient step.

topics.title: [grug] Add the H100 pipeline foundation
topics.body:
Add a stage-local JAXPP pipeline for the full MoE model blocks, including latent/shared experts, SConv, attention positions and QB routing. Standard 1F1B remains the default. The synthetic runner supports the main recipe with FP32 parameters, BF16 compute and compute-scaled MuonH; the historical BF16 capacity recipe remains available.

Each routed expert parameter bank now shares one Frobenius norm across its experts, matching the stacked EP model. `--expert-normalization per_expert` provides an explicit comparison mode. `--qb-bias-mode frozen` retains the current pending QB bias while expert and router weights continue updating; adaptive QB remains the default. Numerical CPU regressions cover stacked-versus-stage-local updates and both QB state transitions.

The historical 48-layer, 65K synthetic diagnostic ran on 192 H100s with BF16-stored parameters and per-expert normalization. Its PP24/EP8/CP1 layout placed two layers in each stage and kept expert traffic within eight-GPU workers. It was chosen to establish capacity; no matched PP8/EP32/CP4 Megatron comparison was performed. The README records the later CP2 result and the differences in batch size and attention helpers. Historical hardware results do not validate the new normalization or frozen-QB option, and no SFT/RL quality comparison has been run.

The affected safe suite passed 2,391 tests with four skips and five expected failures. Focused CPU checks passed 86 tests with one skip; required lint, full type checking, strict docs and source links passed.

#9662 is stacked above this foundation and adds checkpoint/data support, the GB200 launcher, tracked runtime setup and bounded main-recipe hardware validation. Before merge, this foundation still owns replacing the positional result from `initialize_stage_local_pipeline_state`, centralizing the repeated backend/rematerialization identifiers, and separating the synthetic runner lifecycle in `pipeline_smoke.main`. These deferred changes require compiled-startup transport and optimizer-parking/warmup cleanup validation; #9662 then owns adapting its added checkpoint/data lifecycle.

topics.title: [iris] Quarantine nodes with persistent isolated S3 failures
topics.body:
Add opt-in regional S3 read/write/delete probes to the Kubernetes node-agent so a node that remains Ready while storage requests stall can be quarantined before it receives more work. The probe uses the task storage environment, a tiny object per node incarnation, and a process deadline that bounds SDK retries and DNS stalls.

The controller cordons persistent failures only when a fresh majority of nodes successfully probed the same target after the failure began. A persistent cordon budget defaults to one node, and credential/configuration errors reset the failure streak. Node UID, boot ID, report freshness, and Kubernetes resource versions fence stale observations and concurrent operator changes.

Health and cordon evidence remain in node annotations even when Finelog is unavailable. Recovery requires an operator to uncordon the repaired node and release its budget annotation; running tasks are not evicted. Configuration, scratch-object lifecycle requirements, and recovery are documented in the CoreWeave guide.

Context: [node-local storage failure during the hero run](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/599).

topics.title: Score the first 4k Paloma PTB tokens in hero vibe checks
topics.body:
Add `paloma-ptb-first-4k` to the hero vibe-check prompt bank, following https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8827#issuecomment-5723229156. It tracks how the hero scores Paloma's Penn Treebank (PTB) text across sampled checkpoints.

The prompt is the first line of Paloma's `ptb` validation document, a single 399,782-character document with 87,132 tokens under the Marin tokenizer. The prompt is 17 tokens including BOS. The `expected` reference is the next 143 lines, or 4,056 tokens. With EOS, the prompt and reference total 4,074 tokens, within the sampler's 4,096-token `context_length`. Existing expected-answer scoring reports per-token probabilities and the total log-likelihood of the first ~4k PTB tokens at every sampled checkpoint. No code changes are needed. PTB is lowercase, with numbers replaced by `N` and rare words by `<unk>`, so the score partly measures in-context adaptation to that format.

Changing the prompt bank changes the sampling specification and creates a new request for every retained checkpoint. The hourly workflow in `next` mode keeps two jobs active, newest first. Steps 210000 and 204000, the two newest permanent checkpoints of `hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k`, are sampled first. Older checkpoints backfill afterward at the saved priority.

All 47 prompts passed the sampler's prompt-prefix and context checks locally with the pinned tokenizer revision. `tests/hero_vibe_check/test_completions.py` had 19 passing tests. `./infra/pre-commit.py` passed on the changed file.

topics.title: [levanter] Count full-attention layers explicitly in lm_flops_per_token
topics.body:
Count the 26-layer Snowball model's seven full-attention layers in the shared `lm_flops_per_token` estimate. The harness previously counted six, as noted in #9613, because the June trainer used a private estimator with an explicit layer-count argument. The long-layer schedule, every fourth layer plus the last, was also specified in three places.

`lm_flops_per_token` now accepts `num_full_attention_layers`, which takes precedence over the `global_every` stride. The June trainer and Snowball synthetic harness use the shared helper, and the private estimator is deleted. For the Snowball shape, the shared helper matches the deleted function exactly at 4096 and 65536 tokens. The Snowball model exposes `long_attention_layer_mask` for its scan and `num_long_attention_layers` for the harness; the June trainer counts layers with its model's existing schedule function. A test confirms that the harness and June trainer calculate the same FLOPs per example for that shape.

The corrected estimate raises the harness's measured MFU by 0.4% at a 4096-token context. The harness docstring's undercount note is removed.

Part of #9462

---

<details>
<summary>Verification: how the numbers were checked</summary>

All comparisons are exact float equality, not tolerances.

1. **Deleted June helper against the shared helper.** The private `_lm_flops_per_token` from the pre-change `experiments/june_tpu_67b_a2b/moe/train.py` and the shared `lm_flops_per_token` with `num_full_attention_layers=7` were called with the Snowball shape (hidden 2560, intermediate 1280, shared 2560, 26 layers, 20 heads, 5 KV heads, 256 experts, top-4, window 2048, vocab 128256). Results: 5,305,917,440 FLOPs per token at 4096 tokens and 9,735,741,440 at 65536 tokens from both functions. The old stride path (`global_every=4`, six full layers) gives 5,284,823,040 and 9,081,815,040, the 0.4% and 7% undercounts.

2. **June trainer before and after.** `_compute_flops` from the pre-change module and from this branch were run on 36 configurations: layer counts 1 through 12, 24 through 28 and 64, each at the June default shape and at the Snowball shape. FLOPs per example and full-attention layer counts matched in all 36, which also confirms that summing the model's schedule mask equals the arithmetic formula it replaced.

3. **Harness against the June trainer.** `experiments/grug/snowball_synthetic/test_flops.py` builds a June config from the Snowball shape and asserts both estimators give the same FLOPs per example and seven full layers. It runs in CI.

4. **Model behaviour.** `lib/levanter/tests/test_snowball.py` (14 tests, excluding slow, checkpoint and HF cases) passes with the scan using `long_attention_layer_mask`, and the harness tiny preset trains on CPU.

To reproduce item 1 on this branch:

topics.title: [grafana] Add GPU allocation history with explicit gaps
topics.body:
Add seven-day H100 and Blackwell (GB200) allocation panels to Fleet accelerators. Historical values count GPU requests on retained task attempts recorded as Running at each sampling instant, using each child job's resource shape. Both panels share daily Finelog and regional metadata reads. Sampling is one minute up to six hours, five minutes up to two days, and fifteen minutes up to seven days.

The latest retained attempt uses the priority Iris applied at dispatch, including budget downgrades. Older Interactive attempts whose applied band was not retained use unknown priority. Historical counts remain partial and every historical point is marked incomplete: retained data cannot establish when setup pods became assigned to nodes, when lingering pods stopped consuming allocation after controller completion, or the Kubernetes allocatable capacity at that time. Missing allocation stays excluded from the plotted counts; idle remains blank when unverified.

An independent audit of 673 regional emissions over seven days found setup or task-count gaps at 423/673 east H100 samples, 251/673 Reno H100 samples and 450/673 GB200 samples. The other samples still cannot establish complete allocation or idle. The native replay uses 672 common grid instants per model, with 363 H100 and 450 GB200 setup-gap points and 241 fleet metadata-gap points. Running-request reconstruction matched live east H100 (160 GPUs) and GB200 (712); Reno missed an 8-GPU pod that remained Running after its controller attempt finished.

A missing selected regional source produces a blank span instead of a reduced fleet total. Tooltips and coverage expose recoverable setup, metadata and unresolved-model gaps. Cluster Capacity remains the live reference. Finelog producers, schemas, retention and writes are unchanged.

GetGpuAllocationMetadata reads child GPU shapes, requested/current applied bands and attempt lifetimes through existing signed controller federation connections. It includes regional jobs absent from the hub mirror. Verified peers gain this bounded read method; general SQL and transitive forwarding remain denied. Parent and regional controllers must include the RPC before production history loading works.

A Grafana bridge replay with live Finelog and captured regional metadata took 4.94 seconds for initial seven-day loading, 0.009 seconds cached, and 1.39 seconds for current-day refresh. Refresh issued one current-day state query and three metadata reads without repeating the full-week scan. Initial state reads returned 87,655 rows / 9.1 MB Arrow; replay peak RSS was 387 MiB. These measurements exclude production regional RPC latency.

The full Grafana suite passed 419 tests before review fixes; 129 targeted tests and pre-commit checks passed after the fixes. topics.title: Pod creation fails on a node with 65K empty Silo cgroups
topics.body:
On October 2, new pods failed to start on CoreWeave node `g5bc6da`, blocking new jobs. Kubernetes reported `no space left on device` while creating a pod’s cgroup, the kernel group used to track and limit container resources. The node still reported healthy, and its filesystem had 3.55 TB free.

The host cgroup tree had 65,535 descendant groups. Of these, 65,412 were under `/silo`; that entire subtree contained no processes. This strongly suggests exhaustion of the kernel’s roughly 64K memory-cgroup ID space, though we have not traced the failing allocator.

Silo is the nested container runtime running inside our privileged Iris job `muchanem.cap-pipeline-host-53`. Two sampled container IDs from its `containerd-shim` processes matched empty `/silo` cgroups. This points to a cleanup problem in that workload’s runtime, but we have not identified the code path responsible. We have no evidence that CoreWeave’s host containerd created these groups.

Please investigate whether completed containers leave cgroups and shim processes behind, and fix the cleanup path. Verify that repeated container creation and teardown do not keep increasing either count. Coordinate cleanup of the affected node with the pipeline owner; an empty cgroup alone does not establish that it is safe to remove while the runtime is active.

That check requires the workflow ref to be `refs/heads/main` and the source commit to be an ancestor of `main`. The `qualify-x86_64` and `qualify-aarch64` candidate modes build short-lived artifacts on a branch, but they do not publish the candidate manifest required by the release gate. topics.title: [datakit] Score quality from the tokenize stage's token ids
topics.body:
Score quality from the token ids the tokenize stage already wrote instead of
re-tokenizing text in the scoring workers, with the classifier trained on the
marin-tokenizer vocabulary. The stage reads each document's stored `input_ids`
from the tokenize attribute shards, regroups chunk rows, scores begin/middle/end
windows of `max_tokens` ids, and reads the normalize shard's text in lockstep
only for the samples side output. Label text at train and calibration time goes
through the tokenize stage's own per-record encoder, so training ids equal
stage ids byte for byte, special tokens included; a model whose meta tokenizer
differs from the tokenize artifact's is refused with the retrain command.
`train.py` now also fits the calibration, so one command produces the model
dir, and the default model dir and version tag become `pooled_junkgate2_marin`
/ `pooled-junkgate2-marin`.

Measured on the local 35k-document FineWeb-Edu set with a scorer trained on
1,500 Kimi-labeled documents, one worker, JAX on CPU:

| | text path, e5 model | token ids, marin model |
| --- | --- | --- |
| label encoding equals stage ids | n/a | 2,000 / 2,000 documents |
| holdout AUC / Spearman | 0.715 / 0.42 | 0.768 / 0.52 |
| score one shard, wall / CPU | 44.7 s / 115 CPU-s | 6.4 s / 32 CPU-s |
| peak worker memory | 3.1 GB | 1.9 GB |

Output keeps the store contract: same basename as the normalize shard, one row
per document in the same id order, samples carry text. The local full graph
(normalize, tokenize, quality, store, quality report) ran end to end on the
new stage, and on an 8-shard set a rerun after deleting three output files
rescored exactly those 13,121 documents and matched a fresh run file for file. Agreement with the e5
model on the same documents is Spearman 0.77 and 83% within one bucket; it is a
different model on a different vocabulary, reported rather than gated.

The quality step now depends on the tokenize step, so it runs after it per
source instead of alongside it, and it needs reference-pipeline tokenize
outputs at artifact v4. The default model dir does not exist yet: the retrain
on the oracle labels is one command, documented in the fast_transformer README,
and the result has to be staged in gs://marin-us-west4 and gs://marin-eu-west4
before this merges, because the daily datakit canaries resolve the model from
the region prefix and the quality step refuses the e5-era dir. Windows move from 2,000
characters to 512 marin tokens, which covers about the same text for English
and code and less for CJK; the tokenizer revision pin stays identity-only.

topics.title: [grug] Raise hero single-rack MFU from 28.2% to 31.2%
topics.body:
On one GB200 NVL72 rack, these commits shorten the `moe_hero_ep` training step from 13.90 to 12.59 s (28.24% to 31.18% MFU), with loss inside the run-to-run noise of unchanged code. The PGLE profile builder adds no change by default; with a profile built from the program's own trace, the tip before the last two commits ran 12.515 s/step (31.37% MFU, +0.77% over 12.611 without a profile). The changes come from profiling the step's most expensive scopes and from benchmarking OLMo-core 3's BF16 MoE kernels against this path (#9636).

Each row is one run on one rack (`cw-us-east-08a`, 64 GPUs), restored from `hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k` step 180000 with seed 0 for 100 steps, on main's production PJRT wheel. The time is the median step over steps 180011-180099 without the three profiled steps; the gain is the previous row's time divided by this row's, minus one. Repeated runs of the same code differ by about 0.1%. The runs predate the final refactors and review fixes, and the hero's train step lowers to identical StableHLO before and after them.

| Change | Commit | s/step | MFU | Gain |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main | b4d1761ff2 | 13.899 | 28.24% | |
| Remat discounts the host-offloaded carry | 13448300c6 | 13.737 | 28.57% | +1.18% |
| Unfilled ragged transport buffers | a544f2571c | 13.542 | 28.99% | +1.44% |
| Expert-side routing-weight gradient | 9383ef90cc | 13.130 | 29.90% | +3.14% |
| Streaming Triton short convolution | 5600e67b2e | 13.059 | 30.06% | +0.55% |
| SwiGLU backward in the dh GEMM epilogue | c573fecfe0 | 12.943 | 30.33% | +0.89% |
| Device-side kernel availability check | 99d961ed43 | | | no hero change |
| Triton router top-k | 7d28781d70 | 12.875 | 30.49% | +0.53% |
| Token-major dispatch scatter | 3ebb6f91b1 | 12.730 | 30.83% | +1.14% |
| Shared and chunk GEMMs under the MoE transports | a225408148 | 12.638 | 31.06% | +0.73% |
| Synchronous collectives without the carry offload | 7caae09edc | | | no hero change |
| Shared-expert SwiGLU in QuACK epilogues | b24cfe37f8 | 12.652 | 31.03% | -0.11% |
| No routed pre-activation store under remat | 332b1f0b02 | 12.611 | 31.13% | +0.33% |
| PGLE profile builder | 379fdf0e66 | | | no hero change by default |
| End-to-end test that no transport consumer reads unwritten rows | ea02772298 | | | no hero change |
| Short conv and router top-k in Pallas instead of raw Triton | 729a0757f4, fea1451269 | 12.591 | 31.18% | +0.15% |
| Packed bf16 short-conv rounding only on SM90 and newer | 088095b07f | | | no hero change |
| Poisoning test retraces its recompute for each fill | 2b159517c1 | | | no hero change |

The scheduling row bundles three changes that do not stand alone. The MLP-section weight prefetch (from #9481) lets the first shared expert's gate/up projection run beside the first ragged dispatch, but it puts a weight slice behind each layer's carry-offload copy on the same memcpy stream, which stalls the forward by 98-152 ms/step. A barrier that issues the slices before the copy removes the stall; disabling it at the tip slows the step by 0.79%. The shared-expert QuACK row is negative because the scheduling row relies on the shared GEMMs to cover the transports: the 0.18 s/step of compute it saves exposes 0.24 s/step of transport. Removing it from the tip still slows the step, by 0.35% and 0.22% in two pairs.

The last row's gain is against a fresh run of the previous tip, 12.610 s/step, made beside it. Its kernels compile through the same Triton compiler: per call on GB200 the short convolution's forward and backward take 230 and 404 us against 244 and 449 us at 6,144 channels, and the top-k 0.107 against 0.127 ms. Pallas also lets the kernels' tests run on CPU through its interpreter.

Each change that gained less than about 0.3% was removed from the tip and kept only if the tip then slowed by more than 0.2%, with a second pair for results between 0.2% and 0.4%. This dropped a scatter-based inverse permutation (the tip was 0.04% faster without it) and a Triton bincount (0.22% and 0.10%), and kept the pre-activation change (0.47%). The rows from the unfilled transport buffers through the dh-epilogue SwiGLU backward were measured with the inverse permutation in their base; without it, the last of them ran the same 12.943 s.

The unfilled transport buffers, top-k kernel, dispatch scatter and pre-activation change are bitwise, as is the Pallas top-k; the Pallas short convolution keeps its forward and `dx` bitwise, with its weight gradient within fp32 summation-order rounding. The routing-weight gradient, the dh-epilogue SwiGLU backward and the short convolution's weight gradient change at bf16 rounding. The shared-expert SwiGLU now runs on the fp32 accumulator, which changes 0.06-0.3% of downstream routing assignments and stays as close to an fp32 reference as before; the carry barrier moves fusion boundaries. Over 100 steps the tip's loss differs from main by at most 3.8e-4 (2.6e-4 with the profile), against 3.3e-4 between two runs of main.

`moe_mlp` and `MoEExpertMlp` gain `routing_weight_gradient`. The default, `EXACT`, keeps the expert outputs for the backward. `EXPERT_SIDE` takes the gradient from the expert MLP's own backward and skips storing and returning the outputs, but the gradient is zero or inexact wherever `w * dout` rounds to zero in the cotangent dtype, as at a zero weight or a small float16 product. The hero selects `EXPERT_SIDE` (positive sigmoid weights, bf16 cotangents); other ragged users keep `EXACT`.

Peak HBM rises from 103.1 to 123.2 GiB of a 143.75 GiB pool, mainly the 18 GiB routed MoE output the hero saves for the backward; under the carry offload the launcher defaults to `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.78` and slop 105, validated on one rack. A ragged run without the carry offload keeps XLA's default scheduler, which ignores the one-collective limit, so it now runs collectives synchronously; the hero always offloads. A PGLE profile matches one program and mesh, so the production run needs its own before it gains the profile's 0.77%; automatic PGLE stays off. Giving host transfers their own memcpy streams in the PJRT wheel would remove the copy collision for any program; that is left for a follow-up.

This supersedes #9481. It carries that PR's mirror transpose parameters, weight prefetch and PGLE builder, and replaces its two-stage chunk pipelining with the dispatch overlap above, which with PGLE measured 12.666 s/step against 12.783 for pipelining with PGLE on a PJRT wheel without the copy stall, both before the kernels above. Part of #9636; the OLMo-core comparison is on that issue, and the research records are `.agents/logbooks/mfu30.md` and `.agents/logbooks/olmo9636.md` on `research/mcwitt/mfu30`.

topics.title: [eval] Check in the September evaluation campaign
topics.body:
Check in the model, evaluator, and launcher configurations for the September 2026 evaluation campaign, together with the runtime fixes needed for serving, retry, resume, and coverage. The launcher validates external pins, writes immutable effective-config snapshots, and accepts an optional submitter-controlled version label. That label does not attest policy conformance.

Harbor results are bound to the full model and hosted judge configurations, dataset, policy, runtime, and task limit. Resume checks this identity before submission and reuse. A changed checkpoint under the same served name is rejected, as are existing roots without model-bound provenance. Recovery retries known infrastructure failures and unscored trials while retaining scored outcomes and unknown errors.

The frozen Harbor runtime pins 94b118022fe3e677784a638daf33d57a836fa5fe and includes the Tau3 adapter. The Evalchemy lock and generated pin match Marin's external dependency configuration.

SWE-bench uses the native Mini-SWE adapter from merged [Harbor #232](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/232) and [#233](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/233). Its 32,768-token context includes the prompt and reply together. Mini-SWE counts the rendered prompt through the serving tokenizer, including tools and the generation prefix, and caps the reply within the remaining budget and server window. Harbor loads Mini-SWE's base configuration before applying overrides and selects its batch agent, which saves the trajectory on context exhaustion without prompting. Harbor can then verify the existing patch.

Sotopia uses the packaged agent from merged [Harbor #231](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/231). Judge failures become verifier infrastructure errors. The Marin agent wrappers and their harness dependencies are removed. Sotopia's native generation still does not enforce its declared context budget, so those results cannot establish conformance to the 32K context policy.

topics.title: [grug] Keep AdamH updates finite on zero-norm matrices
topics.body:
scale_by_adamh projects onto the parameter's Frobenius sphere by dividing by
the updated matrix norm. A zero matrix stays zero through a zero learning-rate
or zero-gradient step, so the division is 0/0 and the update is NaN. Floor
that norm at 1e-10, the same floor the direction step already uses.

Fixes #9054

topics.title: [fast-track] Marin Belay v1: hill-climb the scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, 8 min on 8×H100)
topics.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. topics.title: Support context-length switches in the hero run
topics.body:
Let the hero switch context length mid-run without changing its training schedule. The ladder launcher takes `--seq-len` and holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, gate/router weight decay, and `run_progress` therefore match the 4K run. A changed context requires an explicit `--qk-mult`, applied to all attention layers; `--capacity-factor` overrides the expert receiver capacity.

Harrier now shuffles blocks of 2^20 tokens (`io_block_size = 2**20 // seq_len`), which equals the existing 256-sequence block at 4K. At a longer context the outer block permutation stays the same, so only each cell's in-progress 512-block window reorders. With the previous sequence-sized blocks, a 16K relaunch would have re-read an estimated 2.85T already-seen tokens of the remaining ~9T. At 16K the past main-mixture boundary moves from step 108000 to 108096, and a continuation must pass `--accept-mixture-boundary-shift`.

Canonical hero eval stays at 4K packing, so the inherited `eval_dropless/*` series remains comparable, and the first-step eval now also runs after a checkpoint resume. Per-example FLOPs rise with context, so a FLOPs baseline (`--flops-baseline-step`, `--flops-baseline-total`) keeps `throughput/total_gflops` continuous across the handoff. `trigger_hero.sh` records the context, QK multiplier, capacity, eval context, FLOPs baseline, and boundary acceptance in the W&B lineage and the #8506 launch record. `launch_diagnostics` gains `--optimizer-tokens-per-step`, `--gate-router-weight-decay`, `--eval-seq-len`, and `--eval-prefix`, so a one-rack rehearsal can use the hero's optimizer settings and report long-context eval separately.

The live run is unchanged. A switch still needs a GPU rehearsal from the handoff checkpoint and agreed trial thresholds; see the inventory and validation plan in #9615.
